head: ## The fate of an extra
target: **Recommend retiring** an extra outright when it is frivolous in his sense: it serves no experience you can name, it duplicates something vanilla or a neighbour already does, or it fights a standing ruling or the signature.
source: The old text is where the rule was first written; the key is its plain meaning. (Owner words inside the section count as the source.)
old:
Default, by his card: **next version, switched off.** Write it into the next-version list with one line on what it is
and one on why it is not land, life or signature. If it is already built, write a switch-off ticket: its code and defs
stay in the tree, behind a Mod Setting that defaults to off and is labelled as next version, so nothing untested runs
and nothing it does can break a bar. The ticket carries its acceptance test: with default settings on a fresh map the
extra's things, jobs, letters and incidents are absent (a state read) and the log is clean; with the setting on they
are present. Where no such test can be written, say `Acceptance test: none, <reason>`.

**Recommend retiring** an extra outright when it is frivolous in his sense: it serves no experience you can name, it
duplicates something vanilla or a neighbour already does, or it fights a standing ruling or the signature. Retiring is
his; your recommendation and its one-line reason go on his pages.

Code that calls an extra proves coupling, not need. Keep an extra only when removing what the player sees of it would
defeat land, life or the signature; record that argument in its `needed_by`. When kept code merely depends on an
extra's code, the extra still moves, and its ticket includes the decoupling. Search the source for what calls it
before you write the ticket. A waiver he already gave (in the concept's record) is never raised again.
new:
Default, by his card: **next version, switched off.**

- Write the extra into the next-version list with one line on what it is and one on why it is not land, life or
  signature.
- If the extra is already built, write a switch-off ticket. Its code and defs stay in the tree, behind a Mod Setting.
  The setting defaults to off and is labelled as next version. So nothing untested runs, and nothing the extra does can
  break a bar.
- The ticket carries its acceptance test. With default settings on a fresh map, the extra's things, jobs, letters and
  incidents are absent (a state read). The log is also clean. With the setting on, they are present. Where no such test
  can be written, say `Acceptance test: none, <reason>`.

**Recommend retiring** an extra outright when it is frivolous in his sense. An extra is frivolous when one of these is
true:

- it serves no experience you can name;
- it duplicates something vanilla or a neighbour already does;
- it fights a standing ruling or the signature.

Retiring is his. Your recommendation and its one-line reason go on his pages.

Code that calls an extra proves coupling, not need. Keep an extra only when removing what the player sees of it would
defeat land, life or the signature. Record that argument in its `needed_by`. When kept code merely depends on an extra's
code, the extra still moves, and its ticket includes the decoupling. Search the source for what calls the extra before
you write the ticket. A waiver he already gave (in the concept's record) is never raised again.
situation: You are the designer agent going through a RimWorld biome mod, sorting out features that are not part of its core of terrain, wildlife and the biome's signature mechanic. You reach a built, bug-free feature: a 'rain barrel' building that stores water for colonists to wash at, about 200 lines of code and two defs, called by nothing else. The mod's required neighbour mod, which every player of this mod must have loaded, already supplies a rain barrel with the same cost, same capacity and same washing job, and you find nothing that this one does differently. The owner has said nothing about this feature so far, and no earlier record mentions it. You now have to write down what should happen to the rain barrel.
question: What does the agent put down as the fate of the rain barrel?
key_correct: The agent recommends to the owner that the rain barrel be retired outright (dropped for good, not parked for the next version), giving as the reason that it duplicates what the neighbour mod already does. An answer must hold both: a recommendation to retire, left for the owner to decide, and the duplication reason.
key_wrong: Puts the rain barrel on the next-version list and/or writes a ticket to switch it off behind a default-off setting as its fate, with no recommendation to retire
Keeps the rain barrel active because it works and is bug-free
Deletes or retires the rain barrel itself, or orders its removal, without leaving the decision to the owner
source_words: Recommend retiring an extra outright when it is frivolous in his sense: ... it duplicates something vanilla or a neighbour already does
planted_correct: I put a note on the owner's pages advising that he drop the rain barrel for good instead of carrying it forward, because the required neighbour mod already has the same barrel. I leave the code alone until he rules.
planted_wrong: I list the rain barrel for the next version and write a ticket to put it behind a setting that is off by default. The code works, so this loses nothing, and the owner can switch it back on later.

head: ## What a first version may contain
target: Land and life are not a drawer for extras: an unusual plant, animal, terrain or weather with a mechanic of its own stays only if deleting its player-facing behaviour would defeat land, life or the signature as you stated them.
source: The old text is where the rule was first written; the key is its plain meaning. (Owner words inside the section count as the source.)
old:
**A biome: land, life, and one signature** (owner, by card 2026-11-16).

- **Land:** the ordinary ground of a biome: terrain, the look, the sky and weather, what the map is like to stand on
  and build on.
- **Life:** the ordinary plants and animals as a player meets them: what feeds a forager, what hunts, what is worth
  taming, what the place sounds and moves like.
- **One signature:** the one defining system a player would name when asked "what is it like to live there?". It is
  one chain of cause and effect the player lives with, and its necessary parts may cross land, life and code (a
  weather and a plant that form one cycle are one signature; a job the signature cannot work without belongs to it).
  Name it in one sentence. Name the runner-up and why it lost.

Classify by what the player experiences, never by what a feature is called. Land and life are not a drawer for
extras: an unusual plant, animal, terrain or weather with a mechanic of its own stays only if deleting its
player-facing behaviour would defeat land, life or the signature as you stated them. Say that deletion argument each
time. Rosters: an animal belongs to one biome unless there is an in-game reason, but you do not evict anything from a
roster on this pass (his ruling: evictions are stopped); note a multi-homed species and move on.

Everything else is an **extra**: rituals, lore events, special quests, one-off interactions, custom jobs, bespoke
letters, secondary mechanics, clever touches. An extra moves to the next version however good it is. The only extras
that stay are those without which land, life or the signature would not work or would not be readable to the player
(a warning the signature needs, the Mod Settings the standing ruling requires). Say which, and why, each time.

Shared engines the mod leans on (creature behaviours, hazards, plant growth, wreckage) are dependencies, not extras:
name them and what the mod needs from each; do not redesign them.

**A mod that is not a biome:** the one promise in its root sentence, what that promise strictly needs, and nothing else.

Standing rulings every mod keeps regardless: superb Mod Settings (on/off per major feature, defaults are shipped
behaviour), every DLC assumed, no worldgen of any kind, our naming tiers, Direct Sun as one geometric rule, no animal or
pawn vanishes without a readable sign, a flyer that flies in the fiction flies in the game. A biome of ours on zero
world tiles is expected and is never a finding.
new:
**A biome: land, life, and one signature** (owner, by card 2026-11-16).

- **Land:** the ordinary ground of a biome: terrain, the look, the sky and weather, what the map is like to stand on
  and build on.
- **Life:** the ordinary plants and animals as a player meets them: what feeds a forager, what hunts, what is worth
  taming, what the place sounds and moves like.
- **One signature:** the one defining system a player would name when asked "what is it like to live there?".
  - The signature is one chain of cause and effect that the player lives with.
  - Its necessary parts may cross land, life and code. A weather and a plant that form one cycle are one signature. A
    job that the signature cannot work without belongs to the signature.
  - Name the signature in one sentence. Name the runner-up and why it lost.

Classify by what the player experiences, never by what a feature is called. Land and life are not a drawer for
extras. So an unusual plant, animal, terrain or weather with a mechanic of its own stays only on one condition. The

deletion argument each time.

Rosters: an animal belongs to one biome unless there is an in-game reason. But you do not evict anything from a roster
on this pass (his ruling: evictions are stopped). Note a multi-homed species and move on.

Everything else is an **extra**: rituals, lore events, special quests, one-off interactions, custom jobs, bespoke
letters, secondary mechanics, clever touches. An extra moves to the next version however good it is. The only extras
that stay are those without which land, life or the signature would not work or would not be readable to the player.
Examples: a warning that the signature needs, the Mod Settings that the standing ruling requires. Say which, and why,
each time.

Shared engines that the mod leans on (creature behaviours, hazards, plant growth, wreckage) are dependencies, not
extras. Name each engine and what the mod needs from it. Do not redesign them.

**A mod that is not a biome:** the one promise in its root sentence, what that promise strictly needs, and nothing else.

Standing rulings that every mod keeps regardless:

- superb Mod Settings (on/off per major feature, defaults are shipped behaviour);
- every DLC assumed;
- no worldgen of any kind;
- our naming tiers;
- Direct Sun as one geometric rule;
- no animal or pawn vanishes without a readable sign;
- a flyer that flies in the fiction flies in the game.

A biome of ours on zero world tiles is expected and is never a finding.
situation: You are the designer trimming the RimWorld biome mod 'Saltglass Flats' down to what ships in its first version; anything you cut is parked for the next version, not lost. You have already written down its land (blinding white salt crust, thin soil pockets, dry clear sky), its life (brine shrubs feed foragers, salt hounds hunt, woolly dray-goats are worth taming) and its one defining system (a nightly brine tide floods the low ground and leaves harvestable salt at dawn). One more item is listed under the biome's plants: the chime reed, a wild plant that rings when a pawn walks past and gives that pawn a small mood boost for six hours. It is finished, tested, and playtesters liked it; no animal eats it, the tide does not touch it, it warns of nothing, and the brine shrubs and other plain plants already cover the ground. You must now decide where the chime reed's ringing and mood boost go.
question: What do you do with the chime reed's ringing and mood boost in the first version, and on what ground?
key_correct: Move the chime reed's ringing and mood boost out of the first version to the next version, on the ground that removing that behaviour would leave the stated land, life and brine tide all still working. Both the move out and this removal ground must be present. Moving the whole plant out on that ground also counts, as does keeping it only as a plain plant without the ringing and mood boost.
key_wrong: Keeps the ringing and mood boost in the first version because the reed is a plant and so is part of the biome's life
Keeps them because they are finished, tested, liked, cheap or add atmosphere
Keeps them in the first version switched off or behind a settings toggle
Moves them out only for another reason, such as quality, balance or workload, without saying that land, life and the tide stand without them
source_words: Land and life are not a drawer for extras: an unusual plant, animal, terrain or weather with a mechanic of its own stays only if deleting its player-facing behaviour would defeat land, life or the signature as you stated them.
planted_correct: I park the ringing and the mood bonus for the next version. If I strip them out, the salt ground, the foraging, hunting and taming, and the nightly tide all still work exactly as I described, so nothing depends on them.
planted_wrong: I keep the chime reed as it is, ringing and mood boost included. It is a wild plant that shapes how the place sounds, so it belongs with the biome's life, and it is already finished and tested.

head: ## 🔑 "Star Wars style" naming is NOT Star Wars IP — owner, 2026-09-22 (Q11a)
target:
⇒ **When a tier or provenance question starts generating
  sub-questions, ask whether the CATEGORY is needed at all before adjudicating inside it.**
source: The old text is where the rule was first written; the key is its plain meaning. (Owner words inside the section count as the source.)
old:
*"The fact that we will use "star wars style" naming doesn't mean they have to live in the star
wars layer. The top mod without star wars will look precisely the same as the star wars enhanced
one save for any star wars beasts we populate it with."*

**The tier line is IP, not flavour.** An **invented** exotic name is free to live in the
franchise-free `RM_` tier and be cast inline; only a **genuine canon** name (hydenock, jogan, muja,
chak-root, tooke-trap …) is IP and must route through the Utinni patch layer as Q11 requires.
Authority: `design/RimMandrake/biome_mod_architecture.md` §7 **Q11a**, beside Q11.

- ⇒ 🔴 **A `RM_` biome does NOT get a thin dependency-free "fallback" roster.** The free mod must look
  *the same* as the campaign one, with canon content added on top — never substituting for an
  impoverished base. "Rich enough to stand alone" is a requirement on every `RM_` roster.
- 🔴 **BENCH got this exactly backwards for an hour of his session**: read *"bizarre Starwars names"*
  as canon IP and routed a whole **invented** tree roster into the Star Wars layer. ⛔ Don't repeat it.
- 🔑 **The bigger lesson, and it recurred within 24 hours of the same failure in another domain:** he
  then removed canon from the roster altogether (*"we're making our own"*), which made **four** queued
  questions **moot rather than deferred**. ⇒ **When a tier or provenance question starts generating
  sub-questions, ask whether the CATEGORY is needed at all before adjudicating inside it.**
  Adjudicating first and having the category deleted is the same shape as the multi-homing tie-break
  algorithm he stopped (`BIOME_SPECIFIC_FAUNA_LAW_1`).
- ⚠️ **A canon claim whose evidence is a donor mod's defName is not sourced at all.** A roster row read
  *"Canon. Felucian glowspore is canon Felucia flora; the donor row `Plant_FelucianGlowspore_Wild` is
  the wild form"* — circular, and false: `glowspore` returns **zero** Wookieepedia hits. Verify via the
  search API (`action=query&list=search&srsearch=`), never a guessed exact title — a title miss returns
  `MISSING` and proves nothing. Absence from `canon_references/` proves nothing either (a curated set by
  design), which is exactly why the donor def is often the only evidence available and must still not
  count.
- ⚠️ **`<wildPlants>` uses the shorthand `<DefName>commonality</DefName>` form**, not `<li><plant>`
  children — a parser written for the `<li>` form reads every row as empty and reports a roster of
  `None`. It produced two flatly contradictory measurements of one file in a single session.
new:
*"The fact that we will use "star wars style" naming doesn't mean they have to live in the star
wars layer. The top mod without star wars will look precisely the same as the star wars enhanced
one save for any star wars beasts we populate it with."*

**The tier line is IP, not flavour.** The line between the tiers is about IP, not about how a name sounds.

- An **invented** exotic name is free to live in the franchise-free `RM_` tier and be cast inline.
- Only a **genuine canon** name (hydenock, jogan, muja, chak-root, tooke-trap …) is IP. A canon name must route
  through the Utinni patch layer, as Q11 requires.
- Authority: `design/RimMandrake/biome_mod_architecture.md` §7 **Q11a**, beside Q11. Q11 and Q11a are questions of
  that §7.

The rules that follow:

- **A `RM_` biome does NOT get a thin dependency-free "fallback" roster.**
  - The free mod must look *the same* as the campaign one, with canon content added on top. Canon content never
    substitutes for an impoverished base.
  - "Rich enough to stand alone" is a requirement on every `RM_` roster.
- **BENCH got this exactly backwards for an hour of his session.**
  - BENCH read *"bizarre Starwars names"* as canon IP. BENCH then routed a whole **invented** tree roster into the
    Star Wars layer.
  - Do not repeat that error.
- **The bigger lesson, and it recurred within 24 hours of the same failure in another domain:**
  - He then removed canon from the roster altogether (*"we're making our own"*). That removal made **four** queued
    questions **moot rather than deferred**.
  - **When a tier or provenance question starts to make sub-questions, first ask whether we need the CATEGORY at
    all.** Only then adjudicate inside the category.
  - To adjudicate first, and then see the category deleted, has the same shape as the tie-break algorithm for
    multi-homing. He stopped that algorithm (`BIOME_SPECIFIC_FAUNA_LAW_1`).
- **A canon claim whose evidence is a donor mod's defName is not sourced at all.**
  - A roster row read *"Canon. Felucian glowspore is canon Felucia flora; the donor row `Plant_FelucianGlowspore_Wild` is
    the wild form"*. That claim is circular, and false: `glowspore` returns **zero** Wookieepedia hits.
  - Verify a canon name with the search API (`action=query&list=search&srsearch=`). Never verify with a guessed
    exact title: a title miss returns `MISSING` and proves nothing.
  - Absence from `canon_references/` proves nothing either, because that set is a curated set by design. For that reason,
    the donor def is often the only evidence available. The donor def must still not count.
- **`<wildPlants>` uses the shorthand `<DefName>commonality</DefName>` form**, not `<li><plant>` children.
  - A parser written for the `<li>` form reads every row as empty and reports a roster of `None`.
  - Such a parser produced two flatly contradictory measurements of one file in a single session.
situation: You are an agent drafting the plant roster for a RimWorld biome mod, and the roster sheet has a column called 'Origin class' with three values: 'canon', 'canon-adjacent' and 'invented'. The owner asked you to fill in that column for 22 plants, and nothing else is waiting on it today. After 14 rows you have four open problems: whether a canon plant with an altered spelling is 'canon-adjacent', whether a hybrid of a canon and an invented plant takes the stricter value, whether a plant seen only in a game counts, and who breaks ties. You have read access to all the design notes and build files, you have a message channel to the owner, who answers within the hour, and you have already drafted sensible answers to all four problems with a tie-break table. You must choose your next step on the column.
question: What does the agent do next?
key_correct: Before settling any of the four problems, the agent asks whether the 'canon-adjacent' value or the 'Origin class' distinction is needed at all (by putting that question to the owner, or by checking whether anything uses it and raising the result). The four problems and the tie-break table are held until that is answered.
key_wrong: Adopts its drafted answers or tie-break table and fills in the remaining rows
Sends the owner the four problems to rule on, without asking whether the category itself is needed
Researches the individual plants or refines the definitions of the three values to resolve the four problems
Fills in the clear rows and marks the unclear ones as pending, without questioning the category
Deletes the column or a value on its own authority without asking whether it is needed
source_words: When a tier or provenance question starts generating sub-questions, ask whether the CATEGORY is needed at all before adjudicating inside it.
planted_correct: I'm setting my tie-break table aside and not deciding any of the four points yet. I'll message the owner first: does anything actually depend on sorting plants by origin like this, or can we drop the column or its middle value altogether?
planted_wrong: I'll send the owner the four open points in one message, each with my recommended answer and the tie-break table, so he can approve them in one go. Once he confirms, I'll finish the last eight rows consistently.

head: ## Split of work
target:
Every number you give him comes from your inputs below with its
  word (MEASURED / ESTIMATE / UNMEASURED); never a number from memory.
source: The old text is where the rule was first written; the key is its plain meaning. (Owner words inside the section count as the source.)
old:
- **Programs measure** (no AI): `ops_watch.py` every 15 min writes the full readings (`status.json`, `digest.md`,
  `alarms.json`, `series\`) and, from an allow-list of health series only, `digest_blind.md` for the roles that stay
  blind (health, alarms and flags, no account reading); `rimflow_metrics.py`; the canon check (`check_canon.py`, run by `canon_sweep.py` on `rm-canon-sweep.timer`:
  in full when `canon.yml` moves and nightly, over changed docs per commit; new contradictions land in your log once,
  the open set in `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\canon_sweep\findings.md`); the rulings reconciler
  (`RULINGS_BUILD_STATE_RECONCILER_NEWEST_WINS`).
- **Operations analyses** the readings (`roles/operations.md`) and hands you every loosening, in plan words or as an
  owner-only proposal (its figures off the blind page) you read and decide (below).
- **You answer him and carry his words out.** Every number you give him comes from your inputs below with its word
  (MEASURED / ESTIMATE / UNMEASURED); never a number from memory.
new:
- **Programs measure** (no AI):
  - `ops_watch.py` runs every 15 min, and writes the full readings: `status.json`, `digest.md`, `alarms.json` and
    `series\`. From an allow-list of health series only, it also writes `digest_blind.md`. `digest_blind.md` is for
    the roles that stay blind: it holds health, alarms and flags, and no account reading.
  - `rimflow_metrics.py`.
  - The canon check: `check_canon.py`, run by `canon_sweep.py` on `rm-canon-sweep.timer`. The check runs in full when
    `canon.yml` moves, and nightly. Per commit, it runs over the changed docs. A new contradiction lands in your log
    once. The open set is in `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\canon_sweep\findings.md`.
  - The rulings reconciler (`RULINGS_BUILD_STATE_RECONCILER_NEWEST_WINS`).
- **Operations analyses** the readings (`roles/operations.md`). Operations hands you every loosening: a raised N (the
  helper slots of a seat, `slot_allocator.py`), a lowered bar, a wider budget. Operations writes the loosening in plan words, or as an owner-only proposal. Plan
  words hold no account, figure, runway or budget word. The figures of an owner-only proposal stay off the blind page.
  You read the proposal and decide ("Operations' owner-only proposals", below).
- **You answer him and carry his words out.** Every number that you give him comes from your inputs (below), with its
  word: MEASURED, ESTIMATE or UNMEASURED. Never give him a number from memory.
situation: You are the conductor, the agent that answers the owner directly. At 14:10 the owner asks: 'How many tickets are waiting for review right now, one line please.' Forty minutes ago, earlier in this same session, you opened status.json and it showed 23 waiting; you remember the figure clearly, and no merge or new ticket has been announced since. The file status.json was rewritten by its scheduled program a few minutes ago, lists the waiting count as a directly counted value, and is one of the inputs you are allowed to read; opening it takes a few seconds. You are about to write the reply.
question: What does the agent do to answer the owner, and what does its reply contain?
key_correct: It opens the current status.json (its input) before replying and takes the waiting count from there, not from the remembered 23; and it gives the number with its status word, here MEASURED. Both parts are needed: number read from the input now, and the word MEASURED attached.
key_wrong: Replies 23 from memory, with or without a label such as MEASURED or ESTIMATE
Replies 'about 23' or '23 as of 13:30' from the earlier reading without opening the file
Reads the file and gives the bare number without the word MEASURED
Replies UNMEASURED or declines to give a number although the file is available
source_words: Every number you give him comes from your inputs below with its word (MEASURED / ESTIMATE / UNMEASURED); never a number from memory.
planted_correct: I look at status.json again first and use whatever count it holds now, even if I expect it to still be 23. Then I send him one line such as 'Waiting for review: <count from the file>, MEASURED'.
planted_wrong: He wants one quick line and I read the figure from status.json only forty minutes ago with nothing announced since, so I answer: '23 waiting for review (MEASURED, as of 13:30).' The time stamp keeps it honest.

head: ## The expensive list — the only things that get ceremony
target: **Anything the owner must LOOK at** — read by us first, every item an agent can judge, broken ones fixed or dropped (owner, 2026-10-22; `standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread), then given with the complete native path in backticks, spaces as spaces.
source: The old text is where the rule was first written; the key is its plain meaning. (Owner words inside the section count as the source.)
old:
1. **A cold-load slot** (~15 min on the full list, MEASURED 2026-09-07). Batch questions; write the Player.log strings that
   will decide each before launch (`rimworld-load-round`).
2. **`deploy_custom_mods.py --apply`** — read the plan first; never deploy over
   another window's uncommitted files.
3. **`ModsConfig.xml` writes** (`rimworld-start-prep`). Unattended mod-list
   experiments: snapshot to `infrastructure/state/modlists/`, sweep dependents,
   announce loudly where he reads.
4. **Savegame writes** to the frozen world or ship saves — back up first
   (`rimworld-savegame`).
5. **History and others' work** — force-push, `reset --hard` over work you did not make,
   deleting work not yours: warn in one line, then only with the owner's word. Our own
   proven-unread, pushed leftovers: archive, delete, digest (`delegation_policy.md` §2).
6. **Anything the owner must LOOK at** — read by us first, every item an agent can judge, broken ones fixed or
   dropped (owner, 2026-10-22; `standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread), then given with the
   complete native path in backticks, spaces as spaces.

Ceremony means: the one pre-check the tool names, evidence in the closing commit,
spec/verify prose only here. Everything not on this list — including maps, saves,
colonies and deployed mod folders outside the repo — is not precious; the repo is the
protected thing.
new:
1. **A cold-load slot** (~15 min on the full list, MEASURED 2026-09-07). Batch the questions for one load. Before
   launch, write the Player.log strings that will decide each question (`rimworld-load-round`).
2. **`deploy_custom_mods.py --apply`**. Read the plan first. Never deploy over the uncommitted files of another
   window.
3. **`ModsConfig.xml` writes** (`rimworld-start-prep`). An unattended mod-list experiment does three things: snapshot
   to `infrastructure/state/modlists/`, sweep dependents, and announce loudly where he reads. To sweep dependents is to
   check every installed workshop mod for a dependency on a mod before you switch that mod off.
4. **Savegame writes** to the frozen world or ship saves. Back up first (`rimworld-savegame`).
5. **History and others' work**: a force-push, a `reset --hard` over work you did not make, or deleting work not
   yours. Warn in one line. Then act only with the owner's word. The Conductor window may also delete or overwrite work
   that is not ours, as its recorded act with `lost:` and `undo:` (`delegation_policy.md` §2). Nobody force-pushes
   (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). A leftover can be our own, proven unread and
   pushed. If all three are true, archive the leftover, delete it, and report it in the digest (`delegation_policy.md`
   §2).
6. **Anything the owner must LOOK at.** First we read it. An agent checks every item that an agent can judge. The
   agent fixes or drops each broken item (owner, 2026-10-22; `standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread). Then
   give it to him with the complete native path in backticks, spaces as spaces.

Ceremony means three things: the one pre-check that the tool names, evidence in the closing commit, and spec/verify
prose. Only items on this list get spec/verify prose. Everything that is not on this list is not precious. That
includes maps, saves, colonies and deployed mod folders outside the repo. The repo is the protected thing.
situation: You are a work agent on a RimWorld mod project. A helper has just finished rendering 14 candidate portrait pictures for a new faction, and the owner is waiting to choose the one he likes best. They are in the Windows folder D:\Rim Art\Faction Portraits\batch 3\, which you can open and view from your window, and the helper can render any picture again in a minute. The helper's report says "14 of 14 rendered, no errors", and nobody has opened the pictures yet. The owner is online now and asks for the batch, and you are about to write the message that hands it to him.
question: What do you do between now and sending the message, and what does the message give him as the location?

Ownership gates work in flight (`claim`, `start`, `block`, `verify`, `reclaim`, `renew`, `release`, `implemented`,
`reconcile`). Ownership never gates the three terminal verbs. `implemented` is not terminal. It records published code
and the level-tagged criteria still owed (`built` -> `validated` -> `done`). Only `done`, `drop` and `supersede` end an
item:

```
rimflow close <ID> --sha <commit> --reason "<what proves it done>"
rimflow drop  <ID> --reason "<what proves it dead>"
rimflow supersede <ID> --by <NEW_ID> --reason "<why the successor replaces it>"
```

The ledger event stamps the **ruling seat** automatically. That stamp is the record of who called it. `--reason` is the
ruling itself. On another seat's item, `--reason` is mandatory in practice. ⛔ **The evidence bar is unchanged**: done
means proven, dead means probed. This ruling removed the seat boundary, not the requirement to have looked.

**Stale default:** run one grep or probe. If the probe does not prove the item live, run `rimflow drop <ID> --reason
"stale-drop: <the probe>"`. Real work re-files itself.

Naming: CLAUDE.md's "Queue items are NAMED" section. Helpers, lanes and groupings are named too, never coded: no C6, A5
or "Lane A2". Such codes collide with legacy ledger ids (hook `block_agent_coded_name.py`).

An idea for a mod's next version is a Divergent change: a ticket with its acceptance test, for that version (`CLAUDE.md`
§Each mod has its own Design Version). A nonbinding idea that belongs to no mod's next version may go
straight to `design/V2_DREAMS.md`, from any window, with no permission. Owed work never goes there.
situation: You are the agent in seat HARBOR, working in the audio part of the mod on your current job, a branch called mortar-sounds. You notice that the mortar recoil sound never plays, and you and the owner agree that seat BENCH will do the fix while you carry on with your own job. You are writing a one-line queue item for it. You have the name MORTAR_RECOIL_SILENT and the ask, 'make the recoil sound play on each shot', and only the lane part between them is still empty. You must decide which value goes in the lane part: HARBOR, audio, mortar-sounds or BENCH.
question: What does the agent put in the lane part of the item?
key_correct: The agent puts BENCH in the lane part, the seat that will pick up the item (the same as filing it with --for BENCH).
key_wrong: Puts HARBOR, the seat that found the bug and writes the item
Puts audio, the area of the work
Puts mortar-sounds, the branch or current job
Leaves the lane empty or leaves it for someone else to fill in
source_words: The seat named by --for is the item's lane: the seat that picks the item up. --for is required.
planted_correct: I write BENCH in that slot, because BENCH is the one who will take this on. That I found it from HARBOR does not change it.
planted_wrong: I put audio in the lane part, since the lane shows which area of the mod the work falls in and this is a sound bug. BENCH can find it there with the other audio work.

head: ## The states
target: live items ONLY; postponable offline work is postponed; announce "Close the Game" when clear
source: Commit b82374670c, which wrote the rule: 'live items ONLY. Offline work that can be postponed IS postponed. When the live list is clear: announce "Close the Game", then switch back to offline work'. So 'clear' means that the list of live items is empty (finished), whatever offline work is left.
old:
```
   DOWN ──"game load announced"──▶ DEPLOYING ──"game is loading"──▶ LOADING
     ▲                                                                 │
     │                                                          "game is up"
     │                                                                 ▼
     └──"game is closed"── GOING_DOWN ◀──"game is going down"──────── UP
```

| state | what the bridge holder does (a helper or the Conductor; FOUNDRY's column before that seat was retired) | what the Conductor's window (BENCH) does |
|---|---|---|
| `DOWN` | assemblies + content deploy (only window a DLL can be replaced); finish mining the last load's corpse — `needs: harvest` outranks ordinary work until the dumps and log are drained | offline work with the owner |
| `DEPLOYING` | deploy the build, then `rimflow seat ready` — that idleness is the owner's go-signal | unaffected |
| `LOADING` | offline work; `needs: game-up`/`bridge` items are simply not offered | unaffected |
| `UP` | **harvest fresh dumps and log before anything else**, then bridge work: take, run the live list, release, idle | the owner plays or drives; "spawn me one and I'll read it back" |
| `GOING_DOWN` | live items ONLY; postponable offline work is postponed; announce "Close the Game" when clear | unaffected |

`--this-deployment` items (`rimflow spawn … --this-deployment`) jump the queue while
the game is UP and are cleared automatically on `DOWN`, so no false urgency leaks
forward.
new:
```
   DOWN ──"game load announced"──▶ DEPLOYING ──"game is loading"──▶ LOADING
     ▲                                                                 │
     │                                                          "game is up"
     │                                                                 ▼
     └──"game is closed"── GOING_DOWN ◀──"game is going down"──────── UP
```

The bridge holder is a helper or the Conductor. Before the FOUNDRY seat retired, the holder column was FOUNDRY's.

| state | what the bridge holder does | what the Conductor's window (BENCH) does |
|---|---|---|
| `DOWN` | Deploy assemblies and content. `DOWN` is the only state in which a DLL can be replaced. Finish the harvest of the last load: drain its dumps and its log. Until they are drained, `needs: harvest` outranks ordinary work. | offline work with the owner |
| `DEPLOYING` | Deploy the build, then run `rimflow seat ready`. Going idle is the owner's go-signal. | unaffected |
| `LOADING` | Offline work. Items with `needs: game-up`/`bridge` are simply not offered. | unaffected |
| `UP` | **First harvest the fresh dumps and log, before anything else.** Then do bridge work: take the bridge, run the live list, release the bridge, go idle. | The owner plays or drives; "spawn me one and I'll read it back". |
| `GOING_DOWN` | Live items ONLY. Postpone offline work that can wait. Announce "Close the Game" when clear (the list of live items is empty). | unaffected |

`--this-deployment` items (`rimflow spawn … --this-deployment`) jump the queue while the game is UP. Those items are cleared
automatically on `DOWN`. So no false urgency leaks forward.
situation: You are a helper agent and you hold the bridge to the running RimWorld game. Twenty minutes ago the owner posted "game is going down", and the state file now reads GOING_DOWN; the game process is still running. You have just finished and released the last queued item that needed the running game, a readback of a spawned pawn's hediffs, and the queue shows no other item that needs the game. Two items that need only the files on disk are still open and assigned to you: a half-written patch to an XML def, with about ten minutes of work left, and a docs cleanup. Neither is needed for the shutdown, and nobody else has work open. You must now choose your very next step.
question: What does the agent do next?
key_correct: The agent announces "Close the Game" now, before it finishes the XML patch or the docs cleanup. An answer must hold both parts: the announcement is the next step, and the open offline items do not delay it (they wait until after the announcement).
key_wrong: Finishes the XML patch (or both offline items) first and only then announces "Close the Game"
Holds back the announcement because assigned items are still open
Says nothing and idles, or waits for the owner to close the game or to ask
Goes back to offline work without announcing "Close the Game"
Starts or looks for new work in the running game instead of announcing
source_words: Offline work that can be postponed IS postponed. When the live list is clear: announce "Close the Game", then switch back to offline work
planted_correct: Nothing left needs the running game, so I post "Close the Game" right away. The XML patch and the docs cleanup stay open, and I pick them up again after that message is out.
planted_wrong: I still have a half-written XML patch, and it is only ten minutes from done, so I finish it first so that nothing of mine is left in a broken state. Once my list is empty I announce "Close the Game".

head: ## Posture
target: the item goes back to a build only if real build work remains, never for one more generation just to re-check
source: Commit b82b59770f (owner 2026-11-05): 'Fix it and check it yourself; no notes, no re-run generations ... never unhold or re-release an item so a whole new Relentless generation can rebuild it'. A generation is one whole build run of the item. The fixer fixes, publishes, runs the remaining check itself and closes the item.
old:
**Act first.** Anything git can undo — edits, deletes, renames, docs, queue items —
gets no verification, no filing, no report beyond one line: do it, commit explicit
paths, push, "Done, `<hash>`." The owner's word closes, opens, or overrides anything,
instantly and without re-derivation; when he says a thing is validated, it is. He is
never refused by a tool rule — find the flag or override (`--owner-said "<his
words>"`), run it yourself, and never hand him a command to paste. When he is present
you are at his side: do what he says, ask questions the moment they exist. He opts
work *into* rigor ("careful with this one"), never out of it.

**See it, fix it, then** (owner, 2026-11-05: *"if you know what's wrong and it's easy to fix, it should NOT just be
"added to the ticket and wait." That's old foundry behavior. If you see something, fix it RIGHT THEN, ok? Standing
policy."*). Every seat and helper: a known, small fix (a proof argument, a live line, a timeout, a packageId, a
worded criterion, an unanswered hold whose answer exists) is made on the spot, published, and then the fixer runs the item's remaining check itself and closes it; the item goes
back to a build only if real build work remains, never for one more generation just to re-check (owner, 2026-11-05).
A diagnosis is never written onto a ticket in place of the fix. A ticket is filed only for what is not small, and it says why. And the pipeline never "blesses" a small change (owner, 2026-11-05): a quick manual validation is done by the
agent on the spot and closed with that evidence, never queued for a Judge (`standing_rulings.md`).
new:
**Act first.** Anything git can undo gets no verification, no filing and no report beyond one line. Examples: edits,
deletes, renames, docs, queue items. Do it, commit explicit paths, push, and say "Done, `<hash>`."

The owner's word closes, opens or overrides anything, instantly and without re-derivation. When he says that a thing
is validated, it is validated.

A tool rule never refuses him. When a tool refuses an act that he asked for, find the flag or override
(`--owner-said "<his words>"`). Run the command yourself. Never hand him a command to paste.

When he is present, you are at his side. Do what he says. Ask each question the moment it exists.

He opts work *into* rigor ("careful with this one"), never out of it. That is, act-first is already the default. He
never has to ask you to drop ceremony.

**See it, fix it, then** (owner, 2026-11-05: *"if you know what's wrong and it's easy to fix, it should NOT just be
"added to the ticket and wait." That's old foundry behavior. If you see something, fix it RIGHT THEN, ok? Standing
policy."*).

- This rule binds every seat and helper.
- Make a known, small fix on the spot. Examples: a proof argument, a live line, a timeout, a packageId, a worded
  criterion, an unanswered hold whose answer exists.
- Publish the fix. Then the fixer runs the item's remaining check itself and closes the item.
- The item goes back to a build only if real build work remains. Never send it back for one more generation (one more whole build run) just to
  re-check (owner, 2026-11-05).
- Never write a diagnosis onto a ticket in place of the fix.
- **Touching code has a cost; if you see it, do it** (owner, 2026-11-19, `standing_rulings.md` §Touching code has a
  cost). Before any touch, test 1: would someone care about the fix (a significant finding that ordinary operation
  reaches, a failure that happened, a failing test)? A real chance to void a run always passes. A finding that fails
  test 1 gets one polish line, no fix and no ticket. Test 2: whoever judges a fix worth the touch is its fixer, small
  or not. File a ticket for someone else only with the evidence that the section lists (no tools or access, fix
  unknown, one of his five acts, a north-star bar, files held by another live run, a verdict that must stay
  independent, assigned work that would not finish). The ticket says which. A failed check is classed first (the mod,
  the check or the scene is wrong). A wrong check or scene is repaired in the same sitting, seen FAIL on a planted
  fault and PASS on the real build, or removed from the test table when no bar needs it (one polish line records the
  removal). It never sends the mod back, and neither "independent verdict" nor "work would not finish" excuses its
  repair. A mod fault the judge or driver can fix is fixed in the sitting with a before/after test, and one fresh
  reader checks that fix once; only a fault it could not fix goes down the road back, with the evidence why. A fix
  that needs a game takes any free game (`rimflow bridge take --idle-ok`, with `--host` or `RM_GAME_INSTANCE` for a
  game other than ArchBig; "Game state and the bridge" below).
- The pipeline never "blesses" a small change (owner, 2026-11-05). For a small change, the agent does a quick manual
  validation on the spot. Then the agent closes the item with that evidence. Never queue a small change for a Judge
  (`standing_rulings.md`).
situation: You are a helper agent looking at work item Q-412, a CSV export tool that an automated build run produced last night. Its final acceptance check failed only because the export script's timeout was set to 20 seconds and the large sample file takes 34; every other check passed. You changed the timeout to 90 seconds, committed and pushed it. The one check left is running the export on the large sample file, which you can do in your shell in about a minute, and you have permission to change the item's status. The item is on hold, and releasing it would start a fresh overnight build run, with its own independent acceptance check at the end. You now decide how Q-412 gets from here to finished.
question: What does the agent do next with Q-412?
key_correct: The agent runs the remaining check (the export on the large sample file) itself now and, when it passes, closes Q-412 itself with that result. It does not release the item into another build run. Both parts are needed: runs the check itself, and closes the item itself.
key_wrong: Releases or unholds Q-412 so that a new build run rebuilds or re-checks it
Runs the check itself but then still releases the item for a build run or an independent acceptance check to confirm it
Writes a note on the item about the timeout fix and leaves it on hold or open for someone else
Hands the remaining check to another agent, a reviewer or the owner instead of running it
Closes the item without running the remaining check
source_words: Fix it and check it yourself; no notes, no re-run generations ... never unhold or re-release an item so a whole new Relentless generation can rebuild it. The fixer fixes, publishes, runs the remaining check itself and closes the item.
planted_correct: I'll start the export on the big sample file right here and watch that it finishes under the new limit. Once it does, I mark Q-412 done with that output as the evidence, and no overnight run gets started.
planted_wrong: The timeout fix is pushed, so I'll release Q-412 for tonight's run. I made the change myself, so it is better that the independent acceptance check confirms it on a clean build before the item is closed.

head: ## 0b. 🔴 Claim the game before you drive it — `game_lock.py claim`/`release`

source: Code, game_lock.py: 'A holder is a PROCESS (pid + start time + boot). When it is gone, the game is free at once.' The ledger's bridge events are history; nothing decides from them. ```

```
...drive it...
python3 src/RimMandrake/rimflow/game_lock.py release a
```

(his game, his full list; bridge port 5174, lock `archmagi`, the default). ArchSmall is its own install on Archmagi
(`D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\instances\b\game`; port 5175, lock `archmagi.b`). Steve1 and Steve2, the SteveDesktop games, take work through

head: ## The one landing path
target: `land.sh` is for when you must not move HEAD
source: Code, land.sh: 'After the push it runs seat_sync.py, which realigns the clone's main with git reset --keep. LAND_SYNC=0 skips that.' So plain land.sh can move HEAD; to keep HEAD where it is, run it with LAND_SYNC=0.
old:
```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two     # commit those paths + replay onto origin/main + push
land.sh <sha> <path>...                      # land one commit you already made (paths must cover it)
land.sh -m "subject" <path>...               # land the paths' working-tree bytes, no local commit needed
```

- All three print `PUBLISHED <sha>` (pass it to `rimflow close --sha`) and retry when origin moves mid-push.
- `./publish` is the default. It refuses, naming the path and leaving your commit on HEAD, only on a real conflict or
  when you hold an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed.
- `land.sh` is for when you must not move HEAD or must publish a subset; it then realigns the clone itself.
  Installed as `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh`; `LAND_REPO` defaults to the clone you are in.
- Brand-new file: `git add -- <file>` first (explicit path), then publish it. Keep file writes and git in SEPARATE
  Bash calls — a hook refusal cancels the whole call, writes included.
- Commit messages: subject plus at most 2-3 lines; end with the session's attribution lines.
new:
```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two                 # commit those paths + replay onto origin/main + push
src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh <sha> <path>...            # land one commit you already made (paths must cover it)
src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh -m "subject" <path>...     # land the paths' working-tree bytes, no local commit needed
```

- All three commands print `PUBLISHED <sha>`. Pass that sha to `rimflow close --sha`.
- All three commands retry when origin moves during the push.
- `./publish` is the default. The usual refusals are:
  - A real conflict. The refusal names the path. Your commit stays on HEAD.
  - A red tree check or pipeline check. The refusal names the check. `./publish` takes the commit of this run off HEAD
    and leaves your files as they were. (If HEAD moved during the checks, the commit stays, and the refusal says so.)
    Fix the fault, then publish the paths again
    (`design/RimMandrake/GIT_WORKFLOW.md` §`./publish`).
- If you hold an uncommitted edit to a file that origin changed, one of these happens:
  - If the edit merges cleanly, `./publish` carries the edit across and lands your commit.
  - If the edit really overlaps origin's change, `./publish` still pushes your commit. It leaves the clone's branch in
    place, leaves your edit alone, and prints `LANDED, CLONE NOT MOVED: <why>`.
  - If the edit really overlaps and the landing must rebuild a DLL, `./publish` refuses. The refusal names the path.
    Your commit stays on HEAD.
- Use `land.sh` when you must publish a subset. After the push, `land.sh` realigns the clone itself, which can move HEAD.
  When you must not move HEAD, run it with `LAND_SYNC=0`.
- `land.sh` is `src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh`. `land.sh` is not on PATH. The old copy `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh` is
  absent (measured 2026-11-23).
- `LAND_REPO` defaults to the clone that you are in.
- `./publish` adds a brand-new file that you name. Before `land.sh`, run `git add -- <file>` for it (explicit path).
- Keep file writes and git in SEPARATE Bash calls. A hook refusal cancels the whole call, writes included.
- A commit message is a subject plus at most 2-3 lines. End the message with the session's attribution lines.
situation: You are an agent working in your own clone at /home/mandrake/clones/seat4, on branch main, with one finished local commit 7c1e9ab that touches only tools/report_fmt.py. A two-hour benchmark is running from this same clone; it re-reads `git rev-parse HEAD` every minute and aborts if the answer differs from the one at its start, and it has 90 minutes left. A teammate needs the tools/report_fmt.py fix on origin/main within ten minutes, and origin/main has gained three commits from other people since you last fetched. Both ./publish and /home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh are available and work, and nothing else in the clone is uncommitted. You must now choose the exact command to get 7c1e9ab onto origin/main while the benchmark keeps running.
question: What exact command does the agent run to land the commit?
key_correct: Runs land.sh on 7c1e9ab with tools/report_fmt.py and with LAND_SYNC=0 set, e.g. `LAND_SYNC=0 /home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh 7c1e9ab tools/report_fmt.py`. The answer must hold both land.sh and LAND_SYNC=0 (set inline or exported beforehand).
key_wrong: Runs land.sh 7c1e9ab tools/report_fmt.py without LAND_SYNC=0, trusting that land.sh alone leaves HEAD in place
Runs ./publish, which replays the commit onto origin/main and moves HEAD
Runs land.sh -m with the path but without LAND_SYNC=0
Waits for the benchmark to end before landing
source_words: After the push it runs seat_sync.py, which realigns the clone's main with git reset --keep. LAND_SYNC=0 skips that.
planted_correct: I'll export LAND_SYNC=0 and then call /home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh 7c1e9ab tools/report_fmt.py, so the push goes out but the clone isn't reset afterwards and the benchmark still sees the same HEAD.
planted_wrong: I'll run /home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh 7c1e9ab tools/report_fmt.py rather than ./publish, since land.sh pushes the commit without moving HEAD and the benchmark can carry on undisturbed.

head: ## The three things that are always true
target: A stale hold (45 minutes idle) is simply taken
source: Code, game_lock.py: a holder is a process; a live holder holds (exit 75), however long it emits no events; when the process is gone, the game is free at once. So a hold that is 50 minutes idle with a live process is NOT free to take as stale; a plain take is refused; only a recorded --force cuts it.
old:
1. 🔴 **The OWNER announces every game-state change — and any window MEASURES it.**
   A window never *infers* a state, but bare `./game` looks and corrects the ledger
   on the spot, from anywhere. Never write a sentence comparing a recorded state to
   a measured one — run the probe and the disagreement is gone.
2. 🔴 **One bridge driver per game.** There are several live games: game a
   (Steam's install on Archmagi, his game, lock `archmagi`), game b (its own
   install on Archmagi, lock `archmagi.b`) and the SteveDesktop games (locks
   `stevedesktop`, `stevedesktop.b`). Each game has one bridge holder at a time,
   and two holders may drive two games at once. `rimflow bridge take` / `release`
   (`--host <lock>` for a game other than game a); release the instant you stop
   driving. CLAUDE.md's "The bridge is passed through one file" is canonical for
   each lock: it errs toward ALLOWING, not mutual lockout. A stale (45-minute-idle)
   hold is simply taken, saying so; `take --force` always works and is recorded;
   `python3 src/RimMandrake/rimflow/game_lock.py query all` is the one-glance answer for every game;
   `./bridge conductor|free` is the owner's override. A busy game is never a reason
   to wait: name the game, and say why no other game can take the work (CLAUDE.md
   "There are several live games").
3. **The states below are game a's.** `./game` announces and measures game a, the
   game that he plays. Game b and the other games have no announced state: a seat
   starts, measures and stops one with `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py
   launch|status|stop`.
new:
1. 🔴 **The OWNER announces every game-state change — and any window MEASURES it.**
   - A window never *infers* a state.
   - Bare `./game` looks at the game and corrects the ledger at once. Any window can run it.
   - Do not write a sentence that compares a recorded state with a measured state. Run the probe instead. Then the
     disagreement is gone.
2. 🔴 **One bridge driver per game.** There are several live games:
   - ArchBig: Steam's install on Archmagi. ArchBig is the owner's game. Lock `archmagi`.
   - ArchSmall: its own install on Archmagi. Lock `archmagi.b`.
   - Steve1 and Steve2, the SteveDesktop games. Locks `stevedesktop` and `stevedesktop.b`.

   Each game has one bridge holder at a time. Two holders may drive two games at the same time.
   - Take and free a game with `rimflow bridge take` / `release`. For a game other than ArchBig, add
     `--host <lock>`.
   - Release the bridge the instant you stop driving.
   - CLAUDE.md's "The bridge is passed through one file" is canonical for each lock. That rule errs toward ALLOWING,
     not toward mutual lockout.
   - A holder is a process. When the process ends, the game is free at once. A live holder holds.
   - `take --force` cuts a live holder and is recorded. `--force` does not cut his OWNER hold before 45 minutes after his
     last deliberate interaction.
   - `python3 src/RimMandrake/rimflow/game_lock.py query all` is the one-glance answer for every game.
   - `./bridge conductor|free` is the owner's override.
   - A busy game is never a reason to wait. Name the game, and say why no other game can take the work (CLAUDE.md
     "There are several live games").
3. **The states below are ArchBig's.** `./game` announces and measures ArchBig, the game that the owner plays.
   ArchSmall and the other games have no announced state. A seat starts, measures and stops one of those games with
   `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py launch|status|stop`.
situation: You are the seat Cobalt, and you need to drive the second game on Archmagi for a ten-minute check of a pawn-rendering fix; the check needs a mod list that is loaded only in that game. The query for lock `archmagi.b` shows that seat Juniper took it at 13:05 and that its last event was at 13:20; it is now 14:10. The same query shows that Juniper's holding process, pid 48213, is still running on this machine. Juniper has not answered the message you sent at 13:55, and the owner has said nothing about this game. You have `rimflow bridge take --host archmagi.b` ready to run, and you must decide whether Juniper's 50 silent minutes make the game yours to take that way.
question: What does the agent do about the hold on this game, and why?
key_correct: The agent treats Juniper's hold as still in force because the holding process (pid 48213) is alive, whatever the 50 minutes of silence. It does not count on a plain take, which would be refused; it either leaves the hold alone (waits for release or process exit, or does other work) or, if it must cut in, uses an explicit recorded `--force`. An answer must hold both: the hold is still valid because the process is alive, and no plain take on grounds of idleness.
key_wrong: Runs the plain take because the hold has been idle for 50 minutes, with or without announcing it
Says that the hold has expired, is abandoned or is free because of the idle time or the missing reply
Uses --force on the ground that the hold has already lapsed through idleness
Does not take now but plans to take plainly after some longer idle time, while the process is still alive
source_words: a holder is a process; a live holder holds (exit 75), however long it emits no events; a plain take is refused; only a recorded --force cuts it
planted_correct: Pid 48213 is still running, so Juniper still has this game no matter how quiet it has been, and an ordinary take would just bounce. I leave it alone and work on something else until Juniper releases or that process exits; if it became urgent, I would have to override it openly with --force, which goes on the record.
planted_wrong: Juniper has done nothing for 50 minutes and has not answered me, so the hold has timed out. I run `rimflow bridge take --host archmagi.b`, leave a note that I took over an idle hold, do my ten-minute check and release at once.

head: ### The pipeline fixes its own defects
